title: UnitedHealth Stock Forecast: UNH Tests $421.87 Fibonacci Resistance as Post-Earnings Rally Extends - FXLeaders
content: Quick Answer: As of Tuesday, October 20, UnitedHealth Group (UNH) was trading at approximately $421.50, up around 3.5% on the day and extending a rebound from the $362.74 October low. The rebound is a continuation of a move stemming from the company’s Q3 results, which it said reflect “the discipline and execution” of its teams. The company also raised its full-year guidance for the third time this year, taking the 2026 adjusted EPS floor to $20.50. On the daily chart, the stock has broken a descending trendline from the July highs and is currently pressing the 61.8% Fibonacci level at $421.87. My view: UNH is bullish as long as it trades above $399.37. A break above $421.87 would likely lead to a target of $440.19 and $458.51. UNH was up around 3.51% on Tuesday, more than double the 1.54% move in the healthcare services and equipment sector. No news was reported to have caused the move. This puts Tuesday’s rally as an extension of the move the stock started on Wednesday, October 14, the day after the company reported Q3 results. For the quarter, UnitedHealth Group reported an adjusted EPS of $4.69, topping the $4.14 consensus, and the company cited “disciplined execution”. As a result, the company raised its full-year guidance to a minimum of $20.50, from its prior range of $19.50 to $20.00. Revenue during the quarter fell to $112.7 billion from $113.2 billion in the same quarter last year. However, earnings from operations improved to $6.6 billion from $4.3 billion, the medical care ratio improved to 88.4% from 89.9% and UnitedHealthcare’s operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.1%. The company has purposely shed members. At the end of the quarter, UnitedHealthcare had 48.3 million members, down from 50.1 million a year earlier, and the company lost 935,000 members in its Medicare Advantage plans since year-end 2025. I would say the quality of the margin is the more interesting question. The current quarter had $610 million of favorable prior-period reserve development. Management also said commercial cost trends are running above its initial 11% assumption, and its 2027 pricing is based on the assumption those costs would continue. In the quarter, Optum Health lost 10% of its revenue to $22.9 billion, largely due to the loss of value-based care patients. But it was still able to improve its operating earnings to $735 million, compared to $41 million last year. Optum’s other units also improved. OptumInsight improved earnings to $1.3 billion from $920 million and Optum Rx improved earnings to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion. Optum Rx now has more than 50 percent of its membership from external clients, further reducing its reliance on UnitedHealthcare members. Operating cash flow of $5.1 billion, or 1.2 times net income, funded share repurchases and the $9.28 annual dividend. According to CFO Wayne DeVeydt on the latest earnings call, analyst consensus for 2027 “may understate the opportunity ahead.” DeVeydt added that a starting point for 2027 might be the low end of the company’s 13% to 16% long-term growth target, which is 13%. With 13% growth on the current $20.50 floor, we would see EPS at $23.17 in 2027, per calculations by Stocktwits. Management has said they will provide a more robust 2027 outlook by year-end. Risks for 2027 are mainly with the company’s Medicare Advantage (MA) business. About 69% of members in 2027 are in 4-Star or greater plans; a reduction from the current year. Plus, about 390,000 members are in MA plans that will not be offered in 2027. Also, two Medicare Advantage investigations by the DOJ remain open. UNH’s stock price, about $421.50, puts it at 20.6 times the 2026 EPS floor and 18.2 times the implied 2027 EPS. Post-earnings targets cluster around these numbers. Baird cut its target to $427, Barclays to $440, and Raymond James to $450, per Benzinga. More bullish targets include $504 from Piper Sandler and $500 from Bernstein, which cut from $512. The stock trades just under the lower targets, and with the latest Q3 beat, and an anticipated 2027 outlook by year-end, I think the upside is greater than the 2027 outlook. UnitedHealth is currently trading at $421.50, a 3.5% gain on the day, and is extending a sharp rebound after dropping to $362.74 in October, which was close to the 200 day EMA. The stock has not only cleared the 50 day EMA at $388.37, but also a descending trend line from the July peak, making the near term trend bullish. One thing worth noting is that price has reached the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level at $421.87, which is often a make-or-break level and in this case could indicate where the recent recovery stops. The 14 day relative strength index (RSI) has hit an overbought level at 72.10, the first time this has happened since May. Similar to the above reasoning, I view this as a caution flag. Above current resistance at $421.87, the next resistance levels are $440.19, which is the Barclays price target, and then the July high at $458.51. The current level of support at $410.51 is also the 50% Fibonacci retracement level. Below that is support at $399.37, which is the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement level, and below that the key level at $388.37 to $385.23, which is where the 50 day EMA meets the 23.6% Fibonacci retracement, and below that is the 200 day EMA and the October low at $362.74. I am bullish as long as UnitedHealth remains above $399.37. A break below that level would put focus on $388.37 and $385.23 and a close below the 50 day EMA would also be bearish. UnitedHealth Group (UNH) extended its post-earnings rally on Tuesday after reporting Q3 results and raising its 2026 guidance for the third time. UNH stock gained about 3.5% on the day, more than double the gain of the healthcare services sector. The key level is the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level at $421.87. A daily close above that level opens up $440.19 and the July high at $458.51. Management has stated they would issue a fuller 2027 outlook by year-end. They have not specified a date, but results for Q4 are expected to be released in late January 2027.

title: UNH Students Speak Amid Lawsuit Challenging Restriction of Using Student IDs to Vote - InDepthNH.org
content:
InDepthNH.org (https://indepthnh.org/2026/10/19/unh-students-speak-amid-lawsuit-challenging-restriction-of-using-student-ids-to-vote/) DURHAM — Some students at University of New Hampshire are speaking out in the wake of a lawsuit that challenges the use of student IDs to vote, expressing concerns that it would cause confusion among young voters and limit their ability to participate in politics. House Bill 323 — which made student IDs a no longer valid form of identification to obtain a ballot — was signed into law by Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte in April. That same month, Secretary of State David Scanlan released a directive advising that student IDs cannot be used as proof of ID when registering to vote, requesting an absentee ballot, or checking in to vote in an election. A lawsuit was filed in August by Free Speech for People, representing Coalition for Open Democracy (a voter education and outreach group) asking the Court to enjoin both HB 323 and Scanlan’s directive before the election. “I believe that student IDs are valid in the court system, and because a student ID is just enough of identification like a real ID would be. I don’t know why you need to bring extra identification… I feel like college students don’t really bring — or have other forms of identification, especially since they have a home, but they’re not there very often — so, they keep all of their identification at home. So, it takes a toll on how many people are able to vote,” UNH student Dalaney Trudeau said Monday. Secretary of State Scanlan’s motion for a stay on the legal proceedings for the lawsuit was denied by the First Circuit Court of Appeals, though an emergency stay has been requested from the U.S. Supreme Court. Previously, a federal judge ruled that student IDs can still be considered by election officials at polling places as evidence of voter identity. They can still be used for considering voter identification if supplemented with other documentation. Head of UNH’s Media Relations Tania DeLuzuriaga said the university has not taken a position on the lawsuit. Michael Garrity, spokesman for the New Hampshire Office of the Attorney General, said there were no updates to the case as of Monday. “The State has asked the United States Supreme Court for an emergency stay in this matter. New Hampshire has a strong interest in ensuring that its election laws are applied consistently and that local election officials have clear, workable guidance in administering elections,” Garrity said. Prime sponsor of HB 323, Rep. Donald McFarlane, R-Orange, did not respond for comment. Co-sponsor Rep. Ross Berry, R-Weare, insisted that the public supports the measure. When asked about the concerns from UNH students that the situation would cause confusion among young voters and how they feel it could limit the amounts of students who vote, Berry said: “I don’t see how that is a thing.” Another student, Olivia Rose of Barrington, said it’s unacceptable and restricting their ability to vote doesn’t seem appropriate. She said it would make students more detached from politics because they won’t feel the need to look into what’s going on politically (and) that limiting their ability to vote and participate in politics would make them less likely to try. UNH student Kai Shanahan said being able to use student IDs is a good way to prove voter identification “because sometimes, students aren’t able to get a driver’s license or a non-driver’s ID. Especially since for a lot of people at college, it’s their first time being out of the house.” Shanahan added she feels it would cause more confusion for young voters in college and “definitely stop people from voting.” According to data from July by the Civics Center — a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization aimed at encouraging young people to vote — noted that just 7% of 18-year-olds are registered to vote in the state as of March 31. It also highlighted how “there is not a single county in the state where the rate was at 10% or more as of March.” The data shows that, per county, the various rates of 18-year-olds registered to vote are: Student James Frady, from Massachusetts, said he wasn’t aware of the lawsuit but if a student ID is supplemented with other forms of documentation to prove voter identification that “I see it as a valid marker that you’re here at UNH and you’re in the system.” “I’m from Massachusetts, and I voted in Massachusetts, but I think it’s definitely a hassle to get all the documents in order. And that could definitely make it easier if student IDs were allowed as an option,” Frady said. House Democratic Leader Rep. Alexis Simpson, D-Exeter said: “Eligible voters have a fundamental right to cast a ballot, and deliberately removing ways to prove identity is voter suppression. For six years, Republicans have made it harder to register, vote absentee, and prove identity at the polls as the cost of living has skyrocketed. If Republicans had an agenda Granite Staters wanted, they would run on that instead of attacking the right to vote.” House Majority Leader Jason Osborne, R-Auburn said he did not have any comments on the matter. title: University of New Haven student killed by wrong-way driver remembered as campus leader - WFSB
content:
NEW HAVEN, Conn. (WFSB) - Ryan O’Shea, a University of New Haven student described as a club hockey captain, fraternity president and campus leader, was killed by a wrong-way driver in North Haven on Friday night. O’Shea, 21, was set to graduate in the spring. He had interned with the NYPD and wanted to become a police officer with the department after graduation. O’Shea was the assistant captain of UNH’s club hockey team. The team had a game Friday night, and O’Shea was driving back to campus afterward. He was on Route 91 South in North Haven just before midnight when state police say 31-year-old Guillermo Carmona-Lopez, of Bridgeport, was driving the wrong way and crashed into O’Shea head-on. O’Shea was then hit by two other drivers and died. Carmona-Lopez is in the hospital fighting for his life. He has not been charged, and state police are still investigating. Ophelie Rowe-Allen, vice president of student affairs at UNH, said O’Shea represented the university well. “Our students are always looking for opportunities on campus to be leaders, good citizens, good stewardesses and to represent the university at all times and that’s what Ryan was doing for us,” Rowe-Allen said. “That was very hard to hear and to know Ryan was coming from a hockey game with his teammates, was very excited and ready for the next game the following day,” Rowe-Allen said. “It’s a very, very sad time for us,” Rowe-Allen said. In a statement, O’Shea’s teammates wrote: “Ryan embodied what it meant to be a Charger. His infectious personality and sense of humor lit up our locker room.” Jackson Brentson, a UNH senior, said O’Shea had an impact on those around him. “I know people who knew him and it seems he had an impact on people and people cared about him and it’s just really awful that something like were to happen,” Brentson said. “I hope the family has a lot of support right now. It’s unimaginable, just awful,” Brentson said. School officials have been in touch with O’Shea’s family. His funeral is set for Friday. The university is setting up travel accommodations for students and offering counseling. O’Shea was from Stony Point, New York, about 40 miles north of Manhattan. O’Shea’s death is the second wrong-way crash death in Connecticut this year. There has been a significant drop in those deaths in recent years: 23 in 2022, 13 in 2024, and seven last year. The Connecticut Department of Transportation has installed 300 wrong-way detection systems on highway on-ramps around the state. The systems have gone off 1,300 times, and in 1,100 of those cases, drivers self-corrected before getting onto the highway. title: Healthcare ETFs to Buy as UnitedHealth Beats on Q3 Earnings - TradingView
content: Shares of UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH have jumped 6.3% on the bourses since the company released better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 13. The healthcare service provider's quarterly figures showed strong financial execution and operational recovery, even as underlying headwinds persisted in the form of membership losses and elevated commercial costs. The company’s chief financial officer Wayne DeVeydt raised 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to at least $20.50 per share, setting a stronger earnings base heading into 2027. Given this upbeat outlook, investors may want to invest in America’s largest health insurer right away. However, given the current U.S. government's legislation last year, which includes major Medicaid funding cuts this year, UNH’s Medicaid business is likely to face significant downward margin pressure. To this end, UNH’s management continues to view 2026 as a trough year for core Medicaid margins. Against this backdrop, prudent investors may be drawn to diversified healthcare exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with significant exposure to UNH, alongside other healthcare giants across pharma, biotech and medtech, as a more strategic investment choice. This would help investors gain from UNH’s upbeat outlook this year while avoiding the risks associated with its Medicaid business. Before suggesting a few such ETFs for your portfolio, let’s take a detailed look at UnitedHealth’s third-quarter performance across key metrics and provide a brief outlook on what to expect in the coming months. UnitedHealth’s third-quarter adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $4.69 beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 13.8%, while its revenues beat the consensus mark by 1.2%. On a year-over-year basis, the company delivered a mixed performance. Its earnings improved 60.6%, but revenues slipped 0.4%. UNH’s adjusted medical care ratio (MCR) was 88.4% in the third quarter, which improved 150 basis points (bps) from the year-ago period. The improvement reflects better medical cost management, benefit and pricing alignment, and care delivery enhancements. Its operating cost ratio improved 70 bps year over year to 12.8% in the quarter, backed by ongoing investments to modernize operations and streamline administrative processes. In its Optum Health business, UNH delivered strong performance in the third quarter, driven by the continued return to value-based care principles, combined with strong execution across its clinical programs and operational improvements, enabling clinicians to focus more on their patients and improve patient experience. As for UNH’s commercial business, the company witnessed stable performance in the third quarter despite a tough market. However, UNH continues to experience higher-than-expected costs for this business, owing to a small number of doctors abusing the dispute process under the No Surprises Act (as mentioned in its third-quarter transcript), in addition to rising costs for specialty drugs and clinician care. UNH expects to pay more than $8 billion in dividends by 2026-end. Meanwhile, to make patient care faster and easier, the company is simplifying its prior approval process by cutting paperwork, increasing transparency and standardizing requirements across the industry. By the end of 2026, UNH plans to eliminate 30% of overall approval requirements, including nearly two-thirds of those for pediatric care and 10% from home health services, while expanding its "Gold Card" program to completely exempt top-performing doctors from routine approvals. Additionally, more than 70% of remaining approvals will be streamlined through standardized electronic submissions, and performance metrics will be published publicly to keep clinicians and members informed. Following UNH’s third-quarter results, Barclays analyst Andrew Mok maintained an Overweight rating but cut the stock’s price target from $441 to $440. Baird analyst Michael Ha maintained a Neutral rating and lowered the price target from $453 to $427. title: What Do History Majors Do? - University of New Hampshire
content: Are you fascinated with how things used to be and what that means for us now? History is the study of the past and how that knowledge can inform the present and the future. This is a broad degree program, allowing you to focus on a particular country, region, time period, or aspect of human culture that interests you, such as religion, science, or cultural movements. You’ll develop the skills in critical reading and writing that form the basis of a solid liberal arts education and prepare you for a wide range of careers, as well as graduate or professional school. Meet William Kirkpatrick '26, a history major from Eliot, Maine, who has found a close community on the UNH campus, with plenty of room to explore by studying how dinosaur bones may have influenced Greek mythology and by studying abroad in Turkey. William Kirkpatrick: I chose UNH because the campus has the appeal of the beautiful small schools of New England while providing enough opportunities, classes, and people to feel like a significant step up from my small Maine high school. Growing up with two parents who worked at UNH, I also had the opportunity to meet some of the professors, faculty, and staff, all of whom were extremely kind and welcoming. It seemed like an easy choice. My favorite thing about COLA is that almost every class I took during my first three years allowed me to explore topics I had never considered before. Coming in my first year, I certainly didn't think I would write a final paper two years later comparing Odysseus in Homer's "The Odyssey" to Mad Max. I can't think of another college that would actively encourage such ambitions. "Almost every class I took during my first three years allowed me to explore topics I had never considered before." I love the history department because of the many subjects it offers. One class will have me writing about medieval hunting practices, and the next will provide the opportunity to present about why dinosaur bones have heavily influenced Greek mythology. I believe, above all, that my liberal arts education has given me the ability to think critically and present my thoughts in a convincing manner after considering the presented material. Paraphrasing Professor Gregory McMahon, a liberal arts education is a lesson in persuasion, critical thinking, and independence presented in the most fascinating way possible. I agree! "I believe, above all, that my liberal arts education has given me the ability to think critically and present my thoughts in a convincing manner." My most impactful professors are both Professor Gregory McMahon and Professor David Bachrach. During my first semester freshman year, Professor Bachrach taught me how to write like a historian and encouraged me to reach out to him with drafts of all my papers. I still refer to some of my papers from that year for format and grammar. Then, in my sophomore year, Professor McMahon helped me understand how fun it is to create new ideas based on ancient sources and supported me when I would come to him with frankly crazy ideas for papers. Professor McMahon sent me to study abroad on his archaeological dig in Turkey this summer. I never took people who said that studying abroad would change your life seriously, because how could it? However, my time in Turkey is one of the highlights of my college experience and probably my life. It's such a vastly different culture from ours, but I fit right in since everyone I met treated me as if they had known me their whole life. In addition to the amazing Turkish culture, getting to see, touch, and excavate the artifacts that I've spent so much of my college career reading about, analyzing, and writing about is a once-in-a-lifetime experience that I can hopefully turn into a twice-in-a-lifetime experience in the near future. "I never took people who said that studying abroad would change your life seriously, because how could it? However, my time in Turkey is one of the highlights of my college experience and probably my life." I received the Trustee's Scholarship coming in my freshman year. This scholarship allowed me to free up money to study abroad in Turkey this summer. I will be forever grateful that UNH allowed me the opportunity to experience Turkish culture from a perspective that many people are not afforded. There are two pieces of advice I would give my freshman self. The first is to explore the campus earlier. There are many cool areas, such as College Woods, the Fishbowl, and the tennis courts, that I never really used until later on. UNH is meant to be explored, and everyone has their favorite spot on campus to study and hang out. The second piece is to study abroad earlier. If I had the chance to go on a second trip before graduation, I would have taken it immediately. I was originally scared that I would feel alone, homesick, and out of place, but I found the opposite was true. There will never be another opportunity to experience international culture like that offered in college, so why not take it? I have found a sense of community within my friend group. Most of us met during the "Become the Roar" tradition during orientation, and we have stayed very close friends throughout all four years. My freshman year roommate is still my best friend, and all of us shared an eight-person suite in Mills Hall during my sophomore year. One thing people might be surprised to learn about me is that during the summers, I work as a groundskeeper for my local cemetery. After someone learns this, I am immediately asked if I bury the people, too, which, yes, I do. However, I am hopefully far from the cemetery groundskeeper stereotype. Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times. Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street’s top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance. Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan. Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. “UNH’s beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher ’26 EPS baseline & upside to ’27 consensus,” said Wright. The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company’s 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026. Furthermore, Wright highlighted management’s view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company’s 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17. Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH’s operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution. Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company’s AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21. Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call. Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse’s current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta’s 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization. “Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta’s core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets,” said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework. While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company’s strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base. The five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell’s Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60. While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell’s XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. title: UNH Vs. HUM: Which Insurer Stock Has More Upside After CMS Reverses Wall Street’s Biggest Medicare Rate Fear? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of UnitedHealth, Inc. (UNH) and Humana, Inc. (HUM) are back in the spotlight on Tuesday after the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) lifted Medicare Advantage payment rates for 2027, with Wall Street estimates pointing to a clear frontrunner. UNH stock rose 8% in extended trading, while HUM stock gained 11%. Over the past year, however, UNH has fallen about 45% and HUM nearly 27%, with both stocks underperforming the broader Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV), which climbed 10% over the same period. The CMS finalized a 2.48% increase in Medicare Advantage payment rates for 2027, up from the January proposal that kept rates roughly flat and wiped out nearly $100 billion in market value across major insurers. The updated policy is expected to add more than $13 billion in additional funding to Medicare Advantage plans next year, the CMS said. With the policy overhang removed, attention has shifted back to valuation targets, which point to higher implied upside for UnitedHealth than for Humana. Based on Koyfin estimates, UnitedHealth carries a 12-month average price target of $357.81, implying a 27% upside from the stock’s last close. Coverage across 29 analysts includes 7 ‘Strong Buy’, 16 ‘Buy’, 4 ‘Hold’ and 2 ‘Sell’ ratings. Earlier this month, Raymond James upgraded the stock to ‘Outperform’ with a $330 price target, citing potential upside from expense trends and expected margin improvement at Optum Health, the company’s care delivery arm. Meanwhile, Bernstein SocGen Group reiterated an ‘Outperform’ rating with a $405 target, pointing to UnitedHealth’s expanding AI strategy. The company recently launched its generative AI companion, Avery, as part of broader efforts to reduce operating costs across its insurance segment, where it plans nearly $1 billion in expense cuts and is closing or divesting about 550 Optum Health clinics. UnitedHealth also expects to lose as many as 2.8 million insurance members this year, with revenue potentially declining for the first time since the 1980s as longtime chair and former CEO Stephen Hemsley leads a turnaround effort. The stock still remains below the level at which Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway built its stake last year and faces scrutiny over Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment practices following a Senate committee review. Humana’s upside appears more modest based on Koyfin estimates, with a 12-month average price target of $212.17, implying a 16% upside from current levels. Among 27 covering analysts, the stock carries 2 ‘Strong Buy’, 6 ‘Buy’, 17 ‘Hold’ and 2 ‘Sell’ ratings. Earlier this year, the company projected adjusted 2026 earnings of at least $9 per share, below consensus expectations of $11.87, while the insurer said margins in its individual Medicare Advantage business could remain just below break-even this year. Several brokerages subsequently lowered price targets, with UBS and BofA maintaining ‘Neutral’ ratings after Humana’s 2026 EPS outlook came in roughly 24% below consensus. On the other hand, Morgan Stanley warned that uncertainty around the size of Humana’s 2026 membership cohort remains a risk “particularly heading into 2027 and beyond.” Cantor Fitzgerald said the stock may remain range-bound until clearer membership data emerges in the second quarter, and Guggenheim said it was taking “a prudent view” of the company’s 2027 earnings outlook. Still, Humana expects enrollment in its individual Medicare Advantage plans to increase about 25% in 2026 compared with last year, with over 70% of new members coming from competing plans. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for UNH and HUM was ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume. One user said UNH “was $600 a year ago. One of the safest blue chips to double In a couple years.” Another user noted that “this $13B increase provides critical revenue relief, offsetting rising medical costs and securing sector stability.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Shares of Hologic (HOLX), Kosmos Energy (KOS) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) touched fresh 52-week highs on Monday, driven by oil-price strength, momentum in AI and fresh dealmaking. Last week, Marvell shares rose 13%, Kosmos Energy edged up about 0.3%, and Hologic ended marginally lower. Hologic shares gained as investors positioned ahead of the company’s planned April 7 takeover by investment firms Blackstone and TPG, after the company said it had received all required regulatory approvals. The deal, first announced in October 2025, values the company at up to $79 per share and $18.3 billion in enterprise value. The company also said its chairman, president and CEO Steve MacMillan plans to retire when the transaction closes. Separately, Casey's General Stores is set to replace Hologic in the S&P 500 index on Thursday as the company prepares to exit public markets following the acquisition. Kosmos Energy shares benefited from rising crude prices amid geopolitical tensions tied to the U.S.-Iran conflict, which lifted sentiment across energy companies. The rally was also buoyed by several analyst upgrades. Last month, Johnson Rice upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ with a $4.25 price target, while Goldman Sachs raised its price target to $2.25. Bernstein said conflicts that extend beyond the early stages “could typically last for years,” adding that given the “uncertainty and right tail risk,” the firm continues to recommend adding exposure to energy. Separately, Mizuho raised its 2026 oil-price outlook by 14% to $73.25 per barrel, saying it was “too early to say whether the conflict raises the structural price of global oil,” but that the bias is “likely higher.” In February, Kosmos agreed to sell its stake in Equatorial Guinea production assets to Panoro Energy for up to $219.5 million, which CEO Andrew Inglis said would “enhance liquidity and accelerate debt reduction” while allowing the company to focus capital on higher-value assets. Meanwhile, Marvell shares jumped after expanding a partnership with Nvidia through the NVLink Fusion ecosystem, boosting the company’s position in next-generation AI infrastructure. Nvidia also disclosed a $2 billion investment in Marvell. Separately, Erste Group initiated coverage of Marvell with a ‘Buy’ rating, citing continued profit growth, improving return on equity and strong positioning in optical DSP and custom silicon used in AI systems. U.S. stock futures traded lower late Monday as traders tracked U.S. President Donald Trump’s deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while weighing ceasefire talks amid elevated oil prices. As of 10.15 p.m. ET, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.8%, while S&P 500 futures were down by 0.6%. Dow futures were down 0.4%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) was ‘extremely bearish’ amid ‘high’ message volume, and sentiment toward the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was ‘bearish’ amid ‘normal’ message volume. Speaking at a White House conference on Monday, Trump reiterated that the U.S. military could target Iranian bridges and power plants if the strait is not reopened by 8 p.m. ET Tuesday. He said negotiations were “going well,” but added that restoring access through Hormuz remains a “very big priority.” He also said that while he would like the U.S. to “take the oil,” Americans ultimately want U.S. forces to return home. The U.S., Iran and regional mediators are reportedly exploring a possible 45-day ceasefire that could open the door to a settlement, while Washington and Tehran are also supposedly reviewing a Pakistan-brokered proposal to restore navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. However, Tehran has said it would only accept ceasefire terms that include a permanent end to the war, sanctions relief, reconstruction commitments and guarantees around safe navigation through the strait. It also warned that strikes on civilian infrastructure could trigger retaliatory attacks on energy facilities across the Gulf. The conflict, now in its sixth week, continues to ripple through energy markets, with West Texas Intermediate settling near $112.41 per barrel and Brent crude closing around $109.77. Michael Cembalest, chair of market and investment strategy at J.P. Morgan Asset & Wealth Management, said that the belief the U.S. economy is insulated from a closure of the Strait of Hormuz is “mostly false,” adding that U.S. fossil-fuel independence “is not as much of an economic firewall as you might think.” In the previous session, the S&P 500 logged its fourth straight session of gains, marking its longest winning streak since January: Investors also weighed weaker-than-expected economic data, with the U.S. services sector expanding at a slower pace in March. The ISM services index fell 2.1 points to 54, with employment posting its sharpest drop since 2023. Broadcom (AVGO): Shares rose 2% in extended trading after the company announced a long-term agreement with Alphabet’s Google to develop and supply next-generation Tensor Processing Units and expand AI infrastructure partnership through 2031 alongside Anthropic. Enovix (ENVX): Shares posted their best session in nine months on Monday as retail traders speculated about a potential catalyst after Chinese media reported a deal with AR-optics firm MoJie to improve battery life in AI-enabled smart glasses. Humana (HUM), UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Elevance Health (ELV): Shares of health insurers rallied in extended trading after the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) finalized a 2.48% increase in Medicare Advantage payment rates for 2027, expected to add more than $13 billion in plan funding. In broader markets, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note hovered near 4.33%, its highest level in about a week. Gold steadied near $4,664 per ounce after a two-day slide, while silver traded around $73.18. Asian markets were mostly higher on Tuesday, with the MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan rising about 0.4%. Shares opened higher in Australia, while Japan opened lower. Among the catalysts for Tuesday are durable-goods orders, durable-goods orders excluding transportation, remarks from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, consumer credit data, and comments from Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson. Revenue rocketed 1,367%, to $4.4 million last year, primarily due to the acquisition of SemiCab India (SMCB Solutions), which concluded in May. Net loss declined 32%, to $16.6 million. With the acquisition of SemiCab, an AI-driven logistics platform that optimizes trucking networks, Algorhythm Holdings has effectively pivoted into a new business. Earlier, it sold karaoke machines and audio equipment. The SemiCab business achieved an annualized run rate of $10 million last year, thanks to five new contract wins with some of the largest multinational fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in India and six contract expansions, the company said in its results statement. In the new year, it has added Coca-Cola India and MTR Foods as new clients. Algorhythm Holdings added that it cut its operating expenses by 20% and reduced liabilities by almost 50% in 2025, and would further improve its balance sheet this year. (TSLA) flashed fresh warning signals on Monday after slipping below key levels following a first-quarter (Q1) delivery miss, with one analyst projecting nearly 40% downside by June as bearish calls built after JPMorgan flagged a major downside to the stock. TSLA stock fell more than 2% on Monday, marking its lowest level in nearly seven months. GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson said on X that Tesla has broken below its 20, 50 and 75-day moving averages and remains trapped in a descending channel that began after the stock’s December highs near $480. He added that Fibonacci levels point to $322 as the next key support, while momentum indicators indicate the stock is not yet oversold. Johnson said investors should watch the $322- $346 range for a potential bounce. The analyst also said that, assuming consensus expectations for negative $1.6 billion in first-quarter free cash flow prove accurate and that prior correlations between Tesla’s free cash flow performance and its share price continue to hold, the stock could fall to $224-$269 by June 30, implying a 24%-36% downside from current levels. He also noted that Tesla’s car sales declined year-over-year in both 2024 and 2025 and are expected to fall again in 2026. “$TSLA has made literally NO PROGRESS on ‘robotaxis’ since launching in Austin in June of last yr. It could fall another 70-80%, and STILL be massively overvalued,” Johnson said, adding that the stock trades as 288x estimated 2026 earnings versus 31x for the Magnificent Seven. Johnson’s technical warning follows a bearish update from JPMorgan analyst Ryan Brinkman, who reiterated an ‘Underweight’ rating and set a $145 price target after Tesla’s Q1 delivery report, implying a 60% downside to current levels. “We ... advise investors approach TSLA shares with a high degree of caution,” Brinkman said. He also lowered 2026 earnings per share (EPS) estimate to $1.8 from $2, below consensus expectations, citing risks to demand, execution and competition as Tesla expands into lower-priced, higher-volume vehicle segments. Future Fund Managing Partner Gary Black said on X, “TSLA bulls out in full force today attacking Ryan Brinkman the person. Yes he’s been wrong on TSLA for 10 years, but he’s been right on TSLA the past five years, so has some credibility.” Separately, Jim Cramer called the bearish JPMorgan call “bold” and speculated that it “must mean people are going to sell this one to buy SpaceX.” His comment follows reports that SpaceX has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering that could become the largest IPO on record, with the company reportedly valued at about $1.75 trillion. Tesla delivered 358,023 vehicles globally in the first quarter, missing Wall Street expectations for a second straight quarter. Deliveries rose 6% from the previous year but fell 14% from a quarter ago, marking the company’s weakest quarter since 2022 outside a Model Y production adjustment period. The company produced 408,386 vehicles during the quarter. Model 3 and Model Y deliveries totaled 341,893 units, while Model S, Model X and Cybertruck deliveries reached 16,130 units. Tesla also deployed 8.8 gigawatt-hours of energy-storage products, down from 10.4 gigawatt-hours a year earlier and below estimates. The results come as the U.S. electric-vehicle market adjusts to the phase-out of federal purchase incentives and competition from Chinese automakers intensifies across markets. Even as bearish calls emerged after the delivery miss, Baird maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating and lowered its price target to $538 from $548, still implying a 52% upside from the stock’s last close, according to an Investing report. Meanwhile, Canaccord Genuity reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating and maintained its $420 price target, representing a 19% upside from current levels following the delivery update. The brokerage noted that rising gasoline prices and firmer domestic used-Tesla pricing could support future demand. I kind of agree with JPM thesis this morning.” Another user claimed that TSLA is “eventually a $40 stock.” TSLA stock has tanked 22% so far this year, ranking as the second-worst performer among the “Magnificent Seven” group of equities. Shares of insurers UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Centene (CNC), Humana (HUM), and Elevance Health (ELV) jumped in Monday’s extended trading hours after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the payments to private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans will increase 2.48% next year. This increase implies $13 billion in additional payments to Medicare insurers for the year, the agency said. “When accounting for estimated risk score trend in MA due to factors such as population changes and coding practices, this amounts to a 4.98% increase,” the agency added. The move came as a surprise since in January, the CMS had proposed a roughly flat increase in payments for private Medicare plans the following year, sending shares of insurers down and wiping out about $100 billion in stock market value. The announcement further comes as a relief to the industry plagued by concerns over rising medical costs. Shares of UNH, CNC, HUM and ELV rallied between 5% and 11% at the time of writing. Shares of Aetna parent CVS Health (CVS) rose by about 6.5% while Molina Healthcare (MOH) stock rose a modest 3%. While UnitedHealth is the largest provider of private Medicare Advantage plans in the U.S., Humana is the second largest.
